headline: Approved variances for a racquet club at 575 Broad Street and a convenience store at 34 Farmington Avenue.
summary: The board approved a parking reduction from 149 to 110 spaces for a racquet club at 575 Broad Street. It also approved a rear yard reduction from 25 feet to 15 feet for a 2,640 square foot convenience store at 34 Farmington Avenue. The board accepted the withdrawal of an appeal for Application #3832 and approved the July 7, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Accepted the letter requesting withdrawal of the appeal for Application #3832, 5-0. The appeal was withdrawn.
Approved a variance reducing the required parking at 575 Broad Street from 149 spaces to 110 spaces for a tennis or racquet club, 5-0.
Approved a variance reducing the rear yard setback at 34 Farmington Avenue from 25 feet to 15 feet for a 2,640 square foot convenience store, 5-0.
Approved the minutes of the July 7, 2026 regular meeting, as amended, 5-0.

Bristol Zoning Board of Appeals Regular Meeting of September 1, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
 
BRISTOL ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
 
 
By: Chairman Rafaniello Time: 6:00 P.M.   Place: City Hall  
      111 North Main Street 
      Council Chambers 
      First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS  PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: Jerald Rafaniello (Chairman) X  
 David Pecevich (Acting Chairman and Vice Chairman) X  
 Rory Ghio (Secretary) X  
 Alfred Radke, III X  
 Liza Salgado-Sirko   X 
    
ALTERNATE 
MEMBERS: 
   
 Jonathan Lukasiewicz X  
 Joseph Kelaita X  
 Mathew Biadun X  
STAFF:  X  
 Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Chairman Rafaniello the meeting was called the meeting to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
Chairman Rafaniello reminded the Commission the next regular meeting was on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. 
 
2. Public Participation 
 
3. Public Hearings 
 
a. Application #3832 – 1. Appeal of the Notice of Decision of the City of Bristol Zoning Enforcement Officer for 
Application B-26-48, for an Interior Fit-Out for a Retail Store at 325 Oakland Street; the Notice of Decision 
publication on March 5, 2026, commenced a 30-day appeal period that ended on April 5, 2026; this appeal 
application was filed on April 29, 2026. 2. Appeal of the City of Bristol Zoning Enforcement Officer's decision 
approving Application B-26-48, for an Interior Fit-Out for a Retail Store at 325 Oakland Street; Assessor's 
Map 24, Lot 236-14; Zone: BG (General Business) zone; OSJ of Bristol, LLC, owner/appellant - PUBLIC 
HEARING POSTPONED FROM THE JULY 7, 2026 REGULAR MEETING. 
 
Acting Chairman Pecevich designated Commissioners Rafaniello, Ghio, Radke, Kelaita and Pecevich to vote on 
Application #3832. 
 
Commissioner Ghio read into the record a letter received dated August 31, 2026, from Attorney Geoffrey W. Millsom 
to Chairman Rafaniello, regarding the request to withdraw the Appeal for Application #3832. 
 
MOTION: Move to accept the letter dated August 31, 2026, requesting the withdrawal of the Appeal for Application 
#3832. 
 
By: Kelaita Seconded: Rafaniello.
Bristol Zoning Board of Appeals Regular Meeting of September 1, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
 
 
For: Radke, Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The appeal is withdrawn.  
 
b. Application #3833 – Request for a variance from Article III, Section 13.2 of the Zoning Regulations to 
reduce the minimum number of parking spaces required from 149 spaces to 110 spaces for a Tennis or 
Racquet Club at 575 Broad Street; Assessor's Map 39, Lot 72; I (General Industrial) zone and BG (General 
Business) zone; Padel Connect CT, LLC., applicant; Bristol NYCEB, LLC, owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Pecevich designated Commissioners Rafaniello, Ghio, Radke, Kelaita and Pecevich to vote on 
Application #3833. 
 
The City Planner noted that the legal notice was correct for the application but the application should have been 
amended to show the I Zone and the BG Zone on the application. The City Planner requested Attorney James Ziogas 
send an email in the morning to amend the application. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, explained the request was an adaptive 
reuse of a non-residential building. Attorney Ziogas noted the applicant wanted to bring a new type of racquet club 
to Bristol called padel-ball with 4 double courts (16 spaces) and 1 single court (6 spaces) with spectator viewing. The 
attorney said the category was discussed and racquet club fit the closest description.  
 
Attorney Ziogas noted 149 parking spaces were required but was excessive because there are existing parking 
spaces. The attorney verified the best amount of parking spaces was a proposed 110 parking spaces.  Attorney 
Ziogas indicated the Regulations required parking that exceeded the ability to create this much traffic.  
 
Attorney Ziogas noted a lot of the trucks would be removed from Liberty Recycling to their own site. The attorney 
specified the parking lot would be paved and restriped and the site would be cleaned up. Attorney Ziogas stated the 
building would be retrofitted and cleaned up for the use. 
 
Yosire Rosenberg of Bristol NYCEB, LLC, 4800 14th Avenue, Brooklyn, NY, explained one of the existing uses of the 
building was for LK Tempered Glass with 80,000 sq. ft. Mr. Rosenberg said there were a lot of tenants in the building 
when the building was purchased. The owner said the LK Tempered Glass tenant required 10 parking spaces for 10 
employees.  
 
Charles Nyberg, architectural consultant, 225 North Main St., representing the applicant, estimated the percentage 
was 50% for the paved and unpaved parking area for the total property. Mr. Nyberg explained the driveway to be 
constructed would access the rear of the site to get to the southeast side of the building because the existing access 
is difficult for vehicles now. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Kelaita Seconded: Ghio. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The Board commented the plan would clean up the property and improve the building and parking areas. The Board 
stated that the classification of the facility was reviewed to the closest category and the required parking spaces 
were on that basis. The Board thought the provided parking spaces was appropriate for the proposed tenant and the 
existing tenants.
Bristol Zoning Board of Appeals Regular Meeting of September 1, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #3833 – Request for a variance from Article III, Section 13.2 of the Zoning 
Regulations to reduce the minimum number of parking spaces required from 149 spaces to 110 spaces 
for a Tennis or Racquet Club at 575 Broad Street; Assessor's Map 39, Lot 72; I (General Industrial) zone 
and BG (General Business) zone; Padel Connect CT, LLC., applicant; Bristol NYCEB, LLC, owner, in 
accordance with the plot plan and information submitted. 
 
By: Ghio Seconded: Kelaita. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
c. Application #3834 – Request for a variance from Article II, Section 8.1.J. of the Zoning Regulations to 
reduce the 25' ft. minimum rear yard abutting a Residential zone to 15 ft. for the construction of a 2,640 sq. 
ft. proposed convenience store at 34 Farmington Avenue; Map 24, Lot 221; BG (General Business) zone; 
Sidhi Vinayak Petroleum, Inc applicant/owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Pecevich designated Commissioners Rafaniello, Ghio, Radke, Kelaita and Pecevich to vote on 
Application #3834. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, explained the applicant wanted to 
constructed a new convenience store to replace the existing convenience store and improve the property. Attorney 
Ziogas highlighted on the west side of the site the diesel fuel pump would be relocated where vehicle enter this area. 
The attorney described the pedestrian concerns with the existing building, canopy, fuel pumps and no parking for the 
convenience store.  
 
Attorney Ziogas added the existing convenience store, rear building and fuel pump (west side of site) would be 
demolished and then construct a new convenience store. The attorney indicated the hardship was the 15 ft. setback 
in the rear yard. Attorney Ziogas stated there would be a new retaining wall with a 6 ft. fence on top of it with 
landscaping behind the fence for a buffer for the neighbors that included a slope.  
 
Board inquires: Attorney Ziogas verified the fuel tanks in the rear yard would be replaced.  
 
James Galella of John Catapano, P.E. of Catapano Engineering & Architecture, P.C., 175 Broadhollow Rd., Melville, 
NY, representing the applicant explained the existing 5 fuel tanks to the rear of the existing building and canopy. Mr. 
Galella said the 5 fuel tanks would be replaced with 3 new fuel tanks in the same location. The engineer outlined 
there would be new parking in front of the proposed convenience store. Mr. Galella overviewed the truck traffic 
pattern that would not interfere with customer vehicles or pedestrians. The engineer indicated the canopy was 13.3 
ft. from the bottom clearance. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Kelaita Seconded: Ghio. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The Board had no concerns with the site layout, setbacks and driving to the rear of the site. The Board agreed with 
the hardship near the rear property line and the safety of the drivers and pedestrians. The Board was in agreement 
that there would be improved access to the site.
Bristol Zoning Board of Appeals Regular Meeting of September 1, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
 
MOTION: Move to approve Application #3834 – Request for a variance from Article II, Section 8.1.J. of the Zoning 
Regulations to reduce the 25' ft. minimum rear yard abutting a Residential zone to 15 ft. for the 
construction of a 2,640 sq. ft. proposed convenience store at 34 Farmington Avenue; Map 24, Lot 221; 
BG (General Business) zone; Sidhi Vinayak Petroleum, Inc., applicant/owner, in accordance with the plot 
plan and information submitted. 
 
By: Ghio Seconded: Kelaita. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting — July 7, 2026 
 
Acting Chairman Pecevich designated Commissioners Rafaniello, Ghio, Radke, Kelaita and Pecevich to vote on the 
July 7, 2026, regular meeting minutes.  
 
Commissioner Radke noted a correction to Pg. 2 to nominate Joseph Rafaniello as Vice Chairman that should state 
Jerald Rafaniello to be nominated as Chairman. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve the minutes of the July 7, 2026, regular meeting, as amended. 
 
By: Ghio Seconded: Kelaita. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
5. Adjournment 
 
Acting Chairman Pecevich designated Commissioners Rafaniello, Ghio, Radke, Kelaita and Pecevich to vote on the 
adjournment. 
 
MOTION: Move to adjourn at 6:54 P.M. 
 
By: Pecevich Seconded: Radke. 
 
For: Radke Kelaita, Ghio, Rafaniello and Pecevich. 
Against: None. 
Abstain: None. 
 
 
This meeting was recorded. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Nancy King 
Recording Secretary 
 
 
 
 
Jerald A. Rafaniello, Chairman David Pecevich, Acting Secretary
